narrative.overview: Ink & Seal treats the app as a carefully printed reading companion rather than a generic media catalog. Warm paper and near-black ink form the quiet field; cover art supplies most of the color; a vermilion seal marks only meaningful status, selection, and action. The interface is comfortably sparse, cover-led, and unmistakably native. The brand layer lives in serif display moments, monospaced metadata stamps, hairline-framed cover plates, and screentone placeholders. System navigation, controls, text styles, safe areas, zooming, and gestures retain iOS behavior.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper and ink surfaces with a complete near-black dark appearance.
A single, scarce vermilion accent inspired by a printer's seal.
Serif titles paired with system body text and monospaced metadata.
Cover-led composition, generous gutters, fine frames, and manga screentone texture.
Native interaction structure with branded details rather than custom platform replacements.

rules.name: The One Seal Rule
rules.body: Vermilion is the only brand accent. Do not introduce competing accent colors for categories or decoration.

rules.name: The Contrast Before Patina Rule
rules.body: Warmth and subtlety never justify unreadable text; strengthen a semantic role before sacrificing legibility.

rules.name: The Editorial Moment Rule
rules.body: Serif belongs to identity-bearing titles, not every label or control.

rules.name: The Text Style Rule
rules.body: Brand type must derive from Dynamic Type text styles; fixed point sizes are not part of the durable system.

rules.name: The Printed Surface Rule
rules.body: If a hairline or tonal step communicates containment, do not add a shadow.

dos: Do let cover art provide the screen's visual variety while the surrounding interface stays calm.
Do use semantic, appearance-aware colors and verify light, dark, increased-contrast, and differentiate-without-color states.
Do derive branded typography and layout metrics from Dynamic Type and available container size.
Do retain native controls, navigation, focus, gestures, and zoom physics.
donts: Don't add gradients, glass effects, competing accents, or decorative shadows.
Don't use vermilion as ambient decoration or for low-priority metadata.
Don't turn every label into uppercase monospaced text.
Don't preserve a fixed phone composition on iPad or at accessibility text sizes.
Don't hide a primary task behind a gesture without a visible and VoiceOver-operable route.
